role: Penrose and Feynman methodological lenses plus current state-of-the-art survey; contemporary model-agent source review, not impersonation, endorsement or external human peer review
scope: Bounded 2024-2026 primary-literature survey for Round32 deliberation loop 1. Extends research/round31/experts/modern/sources.json: records r31-htw, r31-li-tail-errors, r31-mutzel-tilloy, r31-abbott-causal-bootstrap, r31-tsuji-hashimoto, r31-wang-foss-feig-hazzard, r31-rouxinol-neural, r31-penrose-angular-momentum and r31-feynman-cargo-cult are inherited by reference and are repeated below only where they were re-read. No exhaustive reading, no imported theorem admission, no production certificate from this ledger.
search_method: WebSearch discovery followed by direct version-pinned arXiv abstract/HTML opens, institutional pages and one patent full-text mirror. Google Patents, Justia, Espacenet and Lens returned 403/503 through the session proxy; those failures are recorded as leads. Local sanity numerics ran in the session scratch directory only.

field_conventions.reading_depth: abstract | abstract+theorem statements | selected sections | full statement text | metadata only | search summary only | page text | local execution
field_conventions.provenance: arXiv author preprint | journal | institutional page | patent office record via mirror | software registry | community/discourse record
field_conventions.category: a=constructive/Hamiltonian/mass gap; b=local perturbation theory of gapped ground states; c=certified numerics/bootstrap; d=quantum simulation hardware; e=patents and programs; f=discourse; h=historical lens

records.title: Pinched Multi Affine Geometry and Confinement: Describing the Yang-Mills Mass Gap
author: Shoshauna Gauvin
records.section: Abstract (verbatim); Section II.3 'Fixed-cutoff interacting result', Theorem 2.3; Lemmas 2.14-2.15 (creation-operator adaptation to gauge rotors); Theorem 2.5 (thermodynamic ground state); Corollary 2.6; Appendix A.10 title 'Thermodynamic Hamiltonian and complete physical gap'
records.reading_depth: abstract+theorem statements through a rendered-HTML extraction; proofs not audited
records.provenance: arXiv author preprint, general-physics category; no journal reference
records.claim: At fixed spatial cutoff the physical SU(3) Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian a*sum_e L_e + b*sum_p (1-F_p) with b/a <= 1/648 has a unique positive ground vector and H_phys - E >= (8a/3)(I - |Psi><Psi|), volume-independent; reference electric on-site Casimir gap 4/3 (delta = 4a/3), per-site interaction sum J <= 27b/4, J/delta <= 1/128, creation-equation ball radius 1/24, shifted-equation Lipschitz constant < 47/48; thermodynamic ground state with nonnegative generator under exhausting restrictions or periodic cubes; the abstract states the interacting four-dimensional construction, renormalized fields and uniform physical mass gap remain unproved.
records.relevance: Closest external analogue of this project's AM2 finite-volume creation-expansion gap (SU(2), radius 1/64, J <= 28|tau|, gap alpha/16) and of AQ1/AQ2 (thermodynamic state, nonnegative generator). The project's AT4 report already cites v3 Supplement A.10 for the compactness/GNS/Fourier strategy.
records.unresolved_verification: Proofs unaudited; whether Theorem 2.3 was already in v1 (2025-03) or first appeared in v2/v3 (2026-09) could not be checked from the abstract page, so any priority or independence statement between AM2 and this paper needs the skeptic to diff v1 and v3; SU(3) constants do not transfer to SU(2) without recomputing the Casimir gap and star counts.

records.title: Dynamical approach to area law for lattice Yang-Mills
author: Sky Cao
Ron Nissim
Scott Sheffield
records.claim: The Langevin-dynamics approach of Shen-Zhu-Zhu (SZZ23) verifies the Durhuus-Frohlich mass-gap condition in the 't Hooft regime, from which Wilson's area law follows, for G in {U(N), SU(N), SO(2N)}.
records.relevance: Euclidean fixed-lattice-spacing strong-coupling mass gap; same regime class (fixed regulator, strong bare coupling) as this project's Hamiltonian certificates, with a different (Euclidean, probabilistic) method. Useful comparison row for the continuum-trajectory statement: neither approach supplies estimates uniform along g -> 0.
records.unresolved_verification: Parameter regime not mapped onto the AL1 dictionary tau = 96/g^4; body not read.

records.title: Expanded regimes of area law for lattice Yang-Mills theories
author: Sky Cao
Ron Nissim
Scott Sheffield
records.claim: Extends the parameter regimes with proven area law for pure U(N) lattice Yang-Mills beyond Osterwalder-Seiler 1978, via an a-priori bound for the master loop equation and a truncated model handling the merger term.
records.relevance: Documents that the rigorous strong-coupling frontier is moving by loop-equation methods; a possible cross-check target for any future Euclidean finite-graph comparison.

records.title: U(N) lattice Yang-Mills in the 't Hooft regime
author: Ron Nissim
records.claim: Mass gap, unique infinite-volume limit and large-N limit for U(N) lattice Yang-Mills in the 't Hooft regime, via a random-environment SU(N) reformulation combining cluster expansion and Langevin dynamics.
records.relevance: Shows cluster expansion plus dynamics giving uniqueness of the infinite-volume state in a Euclidean strong-coupling regime; the project's goal 4 (state identification) has no Hamiltonian analogue of this uniqueness yet.
records.unresolved_verification: Body not read; Euclidean uniqueness does not transfer to the AQ Hamiltonian subsequential state.

records.title: A scaling limit of SU(2) lattice Yang-Mills-Higgs theory
author: Sourav Chatterjee
records.provenance: arXiv author preprint with journal reference
records.claim: In any d >= 2, SU(2) lattice Yang-Mills coupled to a fundamental Higgs field with degenerate potential has a scaling limit (epsilon -> 0, g -> 0, Higgs length alpha -> infinity with alpha*g = c*epsilon, g = O(epsilon^{50d})) in which a stereographic projection of the gauge field converges to a massive Gaussian field; the non-Gaussian scaling limit remains open.
records.relevance: The only rigorous non-Abelian scaling limit in d > 2 found in this survey is Gaussian and requires matter; it calibrates what the goal-5 continuum statement may honestly claim.

records.title: On the Leading Order Term of the Lattice Yang-Mills Free Energy
author: Christian Brennecke
records.section: Abstract via arXiv listing and search summary
records.provenance: arXiv author preprint with journal reference
records.claim: Leading-order term of the U(N) lattice Yang-Mills free energy on {0..n}^d for all N >= 1, d >= 2, explicit apart from a lattice-Maxwell contribution K_d with axial-gauge boundary conditions.
records.relevance: Weak-coupling rigorous lattice input; the project's AL1 shows its certificate family fails at weak coupling, so this is a lead for what weak-coupling control currently exists (free energy, not gap).

records.title: The heat-kernel master field on Z^d at strong coupling
author: Thibaut Lemoine
records.claim: Large-N U(N) heat-kernel lattice Yang-Mills on Z^d at strong coupling: infinite-volume large-N limits of Wilson loops, factorization, all-order 1/N expansion with exponentially local coefficients, area-law upper bound; via a rooted heat-kernel master loop equation on decorated loop observables.
records.relevance: State of the art for exact strong-coupling loop-equation control; no Hamiltonian gap statement.

records.title: Correlation decay for finite lattice gauge theories at weak coupling
author: Arka Adhikari
Sky Cao
records.claim: Exponential decay of correlations for gauge-invariant functions (including Wilson loop functions) in finite-gauge-group lattice theories at weak coupling.
records.relevance: Finite gauge groups only; a lead for weak-coupling locality methods, not applicable to SU(2) directly.

records.title: The Yang-Mills Millennium problem
author: Michael R. Douglas
records.version_date: Nature Reviews Physics 8, 86-97 (2026), DOI 10.1038/s42254-025-00909-2 (search summaries disagree on volume/pages; one gave '7, 37-121 (2025)')
records.section: Publisher metadata only; page redirected to a login gate
records.claim: Per publisher summary: outlines the problem from a physics point of view, its nature as a mathematics problem, and surveys promising recent approaches.
records.relevance: Current authoritative survey to compare against the project's obligation table; unread here.
records.unresolved_verification: Full text not accessed; volume/page discrepancy unresolved.

records.title: Quantum Yang-Mills Theory (official Clay problem description)
author: Arthur Jaffe
Edward Witten
records.version_date: Clay Mathematics Institute PDF (2022 upload of the 2000 description)
records.section: Extracted text: Section 4 mass-gap definition ('theory has a mass gap Delta if H has no spectrum in the interval (0,Delta) for some Delta>0. The supremum of such Delta is the mass m, and we require m<infinity') and the problem statement ('Prove that for any compact simple gauge group G, a non-trivial quantum Yang-Mills theory exists on R^4 and has a mass gap Delta > 0. Existence includes establishing axiomatic properties at least as strong as those cited in [45, 35].'); Section 5 comment on uniform gap for finite-volume approximations
records.reading_depth: full statement text (pdftotext extraction of the saved PDF)
records.claim: The prize requires existence on R^4 with Wightman/Osterwalder-Schrader-strength axioms and a positive mass gap; the comments note that a uniform gap for finite-volume approximations may matter.
records.relevance: Defines the obligations the project's fixed-lattice certificates do not discharge; anchors the goal-5 statement.

records.title: Clay 'Yang-Mills & the Mass Gap' page; CMSA Millennium Prize Problems Lecture by Sourav Chatterjee
author: Clay Mathematics Institute
Harvard CMSA (event page)
records.section: Clay status sentence; lecture abstract ('A program with this objective, known as constructive field theory, was initiated in the 1960s... Completing this program is the Clay Millennium Prize problem')
records.claim: Problem remains open; recent progress is described as rejuvenating the constructive program, not as a solution.
records.relevance: Provenance for the 'no solution claimed' framing.

records.title: Uniqueness of the Ground State in Weak Perturbations of Non-Interacting Gapped Quantum Lattice Systems
author: D. A. Yarotsky
records.section: Publisher page redirected to a login gate; abstract known through search summary and through HTW's citation
records.claim: For weak perturbations of non-interacting gapped lattice systems, finite-volume ground-state dependence on boundary conditions decays exponentially in the distance to the boundary, implying uniqueness of the infinite-volume ground state.
records.relevance: The theorem behind HTW and the natural target for goal 4 (state identification); AM2 is an explicit-constant finite-volume alternative that does not evaluate Yarotsky's constants.
records.unresolved_verification: Original text not read in this session; hypotheses on site dimension and unbounded on-site terms must be checked before any transfer.

records.title: Ground states in relatively bounded quantum perturbations of classical lattice systems
author: D. A. Yarotsky
records.provenance: arXiv author preprint with journal reference
records.claim: Existence of spectral gap, exponential decay of truncated correlations and analyticity of the ground state for relatively bounded quantum perturbations of classical lattice models; AKLT covered at large scale.
records.relevance: Relative boundedness is the right notion for unbounded on-site Casimir terms; a reference for the second-order (O(tau^2)) expansion proposed for the cap goal.
records.unresolved_verification: Constants existential; not read beyond abstract.

records.title: Local stability of ground states in locally gapped and weakly interacting quantum spin systems
author: Joscha Henheik
Stefan Teufel
Tom Wessel
records.section: Abstract re-read (verbatim); Section 2 and Theorem 3 were read in Round31 (r31-htw)
records.provenance: arXiv author preprint with journal reference
records.claim: Localized but otherwise arbitrary perturbations of weakly interacting systems with uniformly gapped on-site terms change the ground state only locally, even if they close the gap (strong LPPL), as a corollary of Yarotsky's theorem.
records.relevance: Existential constants only; the project needs computed constants, which is why the Riesz-projection/first-order route in the memo is proposed instead of importing HTW.
records.unresolved_verification: Smallness and decay constants not numerically evaluated at |tau| = 10^-8.

records.title: Quasi-Locality Bounds for Quantum Lattice Systems. Part I. Lieb-Robinson Bounds, Quasi-Local Maps, and Spectral Flow Automorphisms
author: Bruno Nachtergaele
Robert Sims
Amanda Young
records.provenance: arXiv author preprint with journal reference
records.claim: Unified quasi-locality framework including infinite-dimensional site spaces and unbounded on-site terms (strong-operator-topology replacements), groundwork for gap stability of frustration-free LTQO models.
records.relevance: The locality technology behind AQ1's thermodynamic dynamics; unbounded on-site terms are covered while interactions must be bounded, exactly the project's structure.

records.title: Quasi-Locality Bounds for Quantum Lattice Systems. Part II. Perturbations of Frustration-Free Spin Models with Gapped Ground States
author: Bruno Nachtergaele
Robert Sims
Amanda Young
records.provenance: arXiv author preprint with journal reference
records.claim: BHM-strategy gap stability under LTQO for perturbations decaying faster than stretched exponential, with 'sufficient conditions for positive lower bounds for the gap that are uniform in the system size and that are explicit to some degree', thermodynamic limit including broken discrete symmetry; GNS Hamiltonian of each pure state gapped.
records.relevance: The phrase 'explicit to some degree' marks the frontier: no evaluated constants at a numerical cap; the project's AM2 supplies fully explicit constants for its own family.
records.unresolved_verification: Body not read; frustration-free LTQO hypotheses differ from the project's product reference.

records.title: On the dynamics of lattice systems with unbounded on-site terms in the Hamiltonian
author: Bruno Nachtergaele
Robert Sims
records.claim: Completes the proofs of Lieb-Robinson bounds and existence of the thermodynamic dynamics for lattice systems with unbounded on-site terms.
records.relevance: Already the AQ dictionary's source for the thermodynamic dynamics; version pinned here.

records.title: Block-diagonalization of infinite-volume lattice Hamiltonians with unbounded interactions
author: Simone Del Vecchio
Jurg Frohlich
Alessandro Pizzo
records.claim: Local iterative Lie-Schwinger block-diagonalization extended to gapped on-site operators plus relatively bounded short-range perturbations (bosons); positive gap for small coupling using weighted operator norms.
records.relevance: An alternative to creation expansions for unbounded settings; its weighted norms are the kind needed for the support-size-weighted anchored norm the memo flags as unproved.
records.unresolved_verification: Body not read; no explicit numerical constants known.

records.title: Stability of invertible, frustration-free ground states against large perturbations
author: Sven Bachmann
Wojciech De Roeck
Brecht Donvil
Martin Fraas
records.provenance: arXiv author preprint with journal reference
records.claim: Stretched-exponential relaxation away from boundaries or impurities for any ground state of the perturbed system, assuming frustration-free invertible reference and LTQO for open boundaries; boundary perturbations need not be small.
records.relevance: Goal 4 (boundary effects): the kind of statement the project would need, with hypotheses (frustration-free, invertible) not verified for the AQ family.

records.title: Local observable errors from truncating interaction tails in gapped quantum lattice systems
author: Kangle Li
records.claim: Ground-state local errors from discarded interaction tails are controlled by the discarded strength near each site, uniformly in system size when the gap persists along the removal path.
records.relevance: Error-organization discipline; not applicable to the project's spatial-volume boundary without an unbounded-site dictionary.

author: Yu Tong

records.relevance: Rigorous representation-cutoff control in real time, complementary to the project's static Round10/11 tail certificates; a lead for a certified dynamic tail bound.

records.title: From estimate to proof: certified ground-state energy bounds for singular Schrodinger operators
author: Xuefeng Liu
records.claim: Verified interval-arithmetic framework with Lehmann-Goerisch quantities giving the first guaranteed two-sided enclosure of the H2+ infinite-domain ground energy (width below 5e-4) with an explicit finite-box restriction error.
records.relevance: Current template for 'domain truncation + certified two-sided eigenvalue bounds'; the project's Round10/11 tail-threshold certificates are the representation-cutoff analogue.
records.unresolved_verification: Software not named in the abstract; body not read.

records.title: Guaranteed Lower Eigenvalue Bounds for Spectral Galerkin Methods with Application to Schrodinger Operators
author: Xuefeng Liu
records.claim: Projection-based guaranteed lower eigenvalue bounds for conforming spectral Galerkin methods; for exact-eigenfunction trial spaces the projection constant is C_N = lambda_{M+1}^{-1/2}, the inverse square root of the first omitted eigenvalue; Kato and Weinstein-Temple need a priori neighbouring-eigenvalue information.
records.relevance: Directly parallels the project's exact omitted-degree threshold (Round11 E4/T1): first omitted eigenvalue controls the truncation; suggests a cleaner lower-bound formula for the finite-graph shift certificate.

records.title: Explicit Two-Sided Eigenvalue Bounds for Schrodinger Operators with Singular Potentials via Finite Element Method
author: Xuefeng Liu
records.claim: Explicit computable two-sided bounds on R^N with singular potentials; the conversion to fully verified interval-arithmetic enclosures is explicitly deferred.
records.relevance: Illustrates the distinction the project already enforces: explicit constants versus executed directed-rounding enclosures.

records.title: Ten Digits on a Train: AI-Assisted Verification of Two Eigenvalue Problems
author: Matthew J. Colbrook
records.claim: Verified zero counts with Dirichlet-Neumann bracketing and a tail-robust Krawczyk-Brouwer inclusion certify eigenvalues to ten digits; AI produced candidates and strategies, some of which failed (an apparently complete tail argument omitted a componentwise check); 'the output is not merely a number, but a number with a proof'.
records.relevance: Documents the failure mode this workbench guards against (AI-assisted arguments missing a component check); supports keeping exact replay and skeptic controls.

records.title: A convergent hierarchy of spectral gap certificates for qubit Hamiltonians
author: Sujit Rao
records.claim: Convergent SDP hierarchy (NPA on the universal enveloping algebra of su(2^n) plus representation constraints, with a ground-energy upper bound as input) certifying lower bounds on the spectral gap of local qubit Hamiltonians, convergent at level n, without frustration-freeness.
records.relevance: A certificate family for gaps that is orthogonal to creation expansions; qubit-only, so not directly usable for rotor sites, but a candidate cross-check on truncated finite graphs.
records.unresolved_verification: Numerical scale of usable levels unknown; body not read.

records.title: Certified algorithms for equilibrium states of local quantum Hamiltonians
author: Hamza Fawzi
Omar Fawzi
Samuel O. Scalet
records.provenance: arXiv author preprint with journal reference
records.claim: Algorithms outputting rigorous lower and upper bounds on local observable expectations in ground and thermal states of local Hamiltonians, with certified convergence in the thermodynamic limit for commuting 2D Hamiltonians at high temperature.
records.relevance: Certified local expectations in the thermodynamic limit is exactly the goal-1/goal-4 shape; hypotheses (finite local dimension, commuting for the fast-convergence result) do not cover the SU(2) rotor family.
